beats.say: The rover landing on Mars's moon Phobos is named after a cartoon terrier.
The Guardian says the Idefix rover is part of Japan's historic MMX mission.
While Phobos is only 14 miles wide, no one has ever landed there.
The spacecraft will reach orbit next August, but the landing is incredibly brief.
The lander will spend only two hours on the surface drilling for material.
It must vacuum up at least 10 grams of soil before heading home.
If this five year mission succeeds, the samples will reach Earth in 2031.
Would you trust a robot dog to find the secrets of Mars?

sources: Japan launches historic mission to Mars's moon Phobos
facts: The rover was named Idefix after the white terrier in the Asterix comics
The MMX spacecraft was propelled by Japan's flagship H3 rocket
Phobos has a diameter measuring 14 miles
This is the first time anyone has attempted to land on Phobos or Deimos
The spacecraft is expected to reach Mars's orbit in August next year
The lander will spend only two hours on Phobos drilling and vacuuming up material
The mission aims to collect at least 10g of soil and rock from the surface of Phobos
The spacecraft is scheduled to return in 2031
